To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the human ether-a-go-go related gene (HERG, the major molecular component for the native rapid delayed-rectifier potassium current IKr, a crucial determinant of the action potential duration) is insensitive to protein kinase A ( PKA ) and PKC phosphorylation per se, but is impaired by the activator of PKA or protein kinase C (PKC) with long exposure, likely via generation of reactive oxygen species ( ROS ).
PKA or PKA activators impair HERG K+ function by increasing ROS generation and that PKA or PC activators impair HERGs function by increasing ROS production.
chronic exposure to PKC or PKA activators impairs HERG function, and that this effect is mediated by ROS production.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of PKA and PRC in HERG channel modulation.
the role of ROS in the modulation of the HERG K+ channels by PKA or PKA phosphorylation.
understanding the molecular mechanisms of the HERG channel regulation by PKA and/or PKC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PKA and PKA activators do not affect the HERG channel function per se but rather by generating the reactive oxygen species.
the chronic effects of PKA and/or PKC activators (or inhibitors) on HERG channel are independent of their direct effects on the PKA- and PKC-phosphorylation of HERG channels.
PKA and PKA phosphorylation do not modulate IHERG, but that PKA and/or PKC activators impair IHERG by ROS accumulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PKA and PKA are not the direct regulators of HERG K channels, but they are the indirect modulators via generation of ROS in pathological condition.
the HERG channel activity is modulated by PKA and/or PKC activation via a mechanism independent of PKA and/orPKC phosphorylation.
the HERG channel is insensitive to the acute modulation of PKA orPKC phosphorylation, but is susceptible to the chronic modulation of PKA andPKC by ROS accumulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the HERG function is not modulated directly by the phosphorylation by either PKA or PKA, but rather by the ROS generation.
the HERG channel function is insensitive to acute PKA or PKA phosphorylation but is sensitive to chronic exposure to PKC activators.

HERG K+ channels are insensitive to PKA and PKA phosphorylation, but can be modulated by chronic exposure to activators of PKC or PKA, which may contribute to impaired cardiac repolarisation in heart failure.
